title: Jim Jordan Asks DOJ to Prosecute Jack Smith Over Alleged Congressional Perjury
excerpt: The House Judiciary Committee chairman accuses the former special counsel of misleading lawmakers about accessing text messages from 44 members of Congress during his Trump investigations.
body:
• Jim Jordan has sent a criminal referral to the Justice Department accusing former special counsel Jack Smith of making false statements during congressional testimony
  • Jordan alleges Smith's team obtained text messages from 44 members of Congress, but Smith denied it during a December 2025 deposition.
  • The DOJ, now led by Trump ally Todd Blanche, says it "will investigate all evidence of criminal conduct."
  • Smith's lawyers call the referral "spurious" and say his testimony was "unimpeachably truthful."

House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan on Wednesday referred former special counsel Jack Smith to the Justice Department for potential criminal prosecution, alleging Smith made false statements during a closed-door deposition about his investigations into President Donald Trump.

In a letter to acting Attorney General Todd Blanche obtained by multiple news outlets, Jordan contended that newly released records contradict Smith's December 2025 testimony that his office did not obtain or review the content of text messages from members of Congress.

"The Committee on the Judiciary writes to refer strong evidence that appears to show Jack Smith, former Special Counsel, knowingly made false statements during his December 17, 2025, deposition."

— Jim Jordan, in a letter to the Justice Department

What Jordan Alleges

During his deposition, Smith was asked whether he sought search warrants for the content of text messages from members of Congress. He responded that he did not recall doing so, testifying that his team had only obtained toll records — logs of incoming and outgoing calls and when texts were transmitted — but not the actual content of messages.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=RI2aTDalyl0

Jordan argued that Smith's responses "gave the impression that neither Mr. Smith nor his team had access to the content of Members' privileged text messages." He stated: "We now know this to be false."

The Ohio Republican pointed to records obtained earlier this month showing that Smith's team received text message content from the National Archives and Records Administration relating to White House personnel phone records. According to Senator Chuck Grassley, Smith's team reviewed text messages from 44 senators and representatives from both parties, though predominantly Republican members.

Jordan specifically asked the Justice Department to examine whether Smith violated 18 U.S.C. § 1001, the federal statute prohibiting false statements to Congress.

Smith's Team Fires Back

Smith's lawyers, Lanny Breuer and Peter Koski, responded late Wednesday with a letter calling the referral "spurious" and describing Smith's testimony as "unimpeachably truthful."

https://x.com/foxnewspolitics/status/2080096239635620192

They argued the distinction matters: Smith's team obtained the text messages through the National Archives' compendium of official White House phones, not through direct search warrants to telecommunications carriers — which is what Jordan's question had specifically asked about.

"The referral is made not because Mr. Smith made a false statement — the letter concedes he did not — but because he did not proactively disclose information that was not responsive to a question asked."

— Lanny Breuer and Peter Koski, attorneys for Jack Smith

Smith's counsel characterized Jordan's action as "a chilling eagerness to weaponize the justice system by attacking a career, nonpartisan public servant who faithfully and fearlessly performed his duties by following the facts and the law."

DOJ Signals Willingness to Investigate

The Justice Department, now under the leadership of Todd Blanche — who served as Trump's primary defense attorney during Smith's prosecutions — confirmed it has received Jordan's referral. A spokesperson said the department "will investigate all evidence of criminal conduct."

The swift response fulfills a longstanding Republican goal. Trump himself has called for Smith to be jailed since returning to the presidency, and Congressional Republicans have pressed for investigations into multiple members of Smith's team.

Ranking Member Jamie Raskin dismissed the referral as political theater. "This referral, if ever brought before a judge, will get laughed out of court," the Maryland Democrat said. "It is meant to harass Jack Smith. It is meant to whitewash their own participation in a scheme to overthrow our elections."

The Broader Context

Smith's investigations into Trump's handling of classified documents and his alleged efforts to overturn the 2020 election results have been contentious since they began. The cases were effectively terminated after Trump's return to the White House, following longstanding DOJ policy against prosecuting a sitting president.

The referral adds another layer to the ongoing dispute over what Republican critics call the "weaponization" of the Justice Department during the Biden administration. Members of Congress have raised concerns for months that Smith's use of subpoenas to access their communications records violated the Speech or Debate Clause of the Constitution, which protects legislative communications.

Smith's lawyers countered that the clause "does not prevent prosecutors from using or reviewing text messages between Members of Congress and members of the Executive Branch in an investigation and prosecution of an Executive Branch official, which is precisely what happened here."

Criminal referrals from Congress to the Justice Department are common but rarely result in prosecution. Whether the current DOJ will pursue charges against Smith remains an open question — though with Trump's allies now controlling the department, the political dynamics have shifted markedly since Smith completed his work.
image_caption: Former Special Counsel Jack Smith during his tenure leading the investigations into President Donald Trump. Jordan alleges Smith misled Congress about accessing lawmakers' text messages during his probes.
nri_angle: The referral intensifies the ongoing partisan battle over the Justice Department's independence, a debate that has resonated with Indian-American political observers following the community's growing engagement in U.S. politics.
